es: Reconocer en una propuesta de barrio sus cuatro partes (objetivo, beneficio, plan y petición) y los verbos que sugieren y justifican.

teaching.en: The objective of this proposal is to turn the empty square into a weekend market where local growers can rent a stall, and every stakeholder has been consulted.
teaching.es: El objetivo de esta propuesta es convertir la plaza vacía en un mercado de fin de semana donde los productores locales puedan alquilar un puesto, y se ha consultado a todas las partes interesadas.
teaching.explanationEs: The objective is to… abre la propuesta y dice qué se quiere lograr.
segments: The objective of this proposal is to turn the empty square into a weekend
market where local growers can rent a stall, and every stakeholder has been consulted.
teaching.audioText: The objective of this proposal is to turn the empty square into a weekend market where local growers can rent a stall, and every stakeholder has been consulted.

teaching.en: The most tangible benefit is that families will finally have a safe place to meet, something the neighbourhood has lacked for years.
teaching.es: El beneficio más tangible es que las familias por fin tendrán un lugar seguro donde reunirse, algo que al barrio le ha faltado durante años.
teaching.explanationEs: Tangible benefit: una ventaja concreta que se puede ver o medir, no una promesa vaga.
segments: The most tangible benefit is that families will finally have a
safe place to meet, something the neighbourhood has lacked for years.
teaching.audioText: The most tangible benefit is that families will finally have a safe place to meet, something the neighbourhood has lacked for years.

teaching.en: We outline three stages: clearing the square in April, building twenty stalls in May and opening to the public in June.
teaching.es: Esbozamos tres etapas: limpiar la plaza en abril, montar veinte puestos en mayo y abrir al público en junio.
teaching.explanationEs: We outline… presenta el plan a grandes rasgos, en pasos ordenados.
segments: We outline three stages: clearing the square in April, building twenty
stalls in May and opening to the public in June.
teaching.audioText: We outline three stages: clearing the square in April, building twenty stalls in May and opening to the public in June.

teaching.en: After weighing the costs, we recommend holding the market on Saturdays, because that is when most residents are free, which gives the proposal a compelling argument.
teaching.es: Tras sopesar los costos, recomendamos celebrar el mercado los sábados, porque es cuando casi todos los vecinos están libres, lo que da a la propuesta un argumento convincente.
teaching.explanationEs: We recommend + -ing: el autor aconseja y justifica en la misma frase.
segments: After weighing the costs, we recommend holding the market on Saturdays, because that
is when most residents are free, which gives the proposal a compelling argument.
teaching.audioText: After weighing the costs, we recommend holding the market on Saturdays, because that is when most residents are free, which gives the proposal a compelling argument.

teaching.en: We respectfully request a grant of 4,000 dollars from the council, which would cover the cost of the stalls and the insurance.
teaching.es: Solicitamos respetuosamente una subvención de 4.000 dólares al consejo, que cubriría el costo de los puestos y del seguro.
teaching.explanationEs: We request… formula la petición, casi siempre al final y con tono cortés.
segments: We respectfully request a grant of 4,000 dollars from the council,
which would cover the cost of the stalls and the insurance.
teaching.audioText: We respectfully request a grant of 4,000 dollars from the council, which would cover the cost of the stalls and the insurance.

teaching.en: Tonight Ana will give a short pitch to put forward the idea, and two shop owners will endorse it, but the written proposal has every detail.
teaching.es: Esta noche Ana hará una presentación breve para plantear la idea y dos comerciantes la respaldarán, pero la propuesta escrita tiene todos los detalles.
teaching.explanationEs: Pitch es la versión oral y corta; put forward = plantear una idea; endorse = respaldarla públicamente.
segments: Tonight Ana will give a short pitch to put forward the idea, and
two shop owners will endorse it, but the written proposal has every detail.
teaching.audioText: Tonight Ana will give a short pitch to put forward the idea, and two shop owners will endorse it, but the written proposal has every detail.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte de una propuesta es este párrafo del borrador?

choices.text: It states the objective of the project.
It lists the benefits for local residents.
It makes a formal request for money.

feedback.es: El párrafo dice qué se quiere lograr («Our aim is to turn…»): es el objetivo, no la lista de beneficios ni una petición.

hint.es: Busca qué quiere conseguir el proyecto; no hay cifras ni dinero solicitado.

origin.text: Young people in the neighbourhood have nowhere to meet after school, and the bus service stops at six. Our aim is to turn the old depot into a workshop where teenagers can learn practical skills.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo es dar a los jóvenes un sitio donde aprender oficios.»

feedback.es: The objective is to + verbo base nombra lo que la propuesta quiere lograr.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que abre la propuesta y nombra lo que se quiere lograr.

origin.text: The proposal is to turn the old depot into a youth workshop. The ___ is to give teenagers somewhere to learn practical skills after school.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esta noche Ana planteará nuestra propuesta ante el consejo.»

answer.text: Tonight Ana will put forward our proposal to the council

feedback.es: Put forward + la idea o la propuesta significa plantearla ante un órgano o un público.

hint.es: Empieza por el adverbio de tiempo y deja al consejo para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué petición hace el equipo al final.

choices.text: Permission to use the library building on Saturdays.
Money from the council to help pay for the market.
Twenty volunteers to build the stalls in May.

feedback.es: La petición llega en la última frase: «we request a grant… from the council»; la biblioteca solo da nombre al lugar y los voluntarios no se mencionan.

origin.audio: Good evening, everyone. Our objective is to turn the empty car park behind the library into a weekend market with twenty stalls. The main benefit is tangible: local growers will earn a fair income, and families will have somewhere safe to meet. We outline three stages: clearing the site in April, building the stalls in May and opening in June. We recommend holding the market on Saturdays, when most residents are free. Finally, we request a grant of four thousand dollars from the council.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una propuesta con la parte que cumple.

pairs: The objective is to reduce litter on the riverside path.
The most tangible benefit is that children will walk to school safely.
We outline two stages: clearing in spring and planting in autumn.
We respectfully request a grant of 2,000 dollars.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula delata su parte: objective (qué), benefit (para quién), outline (cómo) y request (qué se pide).

pairs: The objective is to reduce litter on the riverside path.
The most tangible benefit is that children will walk to school safely.
We outline two stages: clearing in spring and planting in autumn.
We respectfully request a grant of 2,000 dollars.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso. ¿Qué diferencia se da a entender entre el pitch y la propuesta escrita?

choices.text: The pitch replaces the document, so nobody needs to read it.
The document summarises what Ana will say on Thursday.
The pitch only introduces the idea; the document holds the detail.

feedback.es: El pitch es breve y sirve para plantear la idea; los datos completos (presupuesto y calendario) están en el documento escrito.

origin.text: Notice: On Thursday Ana will put forward the idea in a five-minute pitch. The full proposal, with the budget and the calendar, will be available on paper at the library from Friday.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué finalidad escribe Mia este correo?

choices.text: To ask for funding and support for a book swap.
To announce that the book swap has been approved.
To complain that the library is used too little.

feedback.es: Mia plantea una propuesta y pide una subvención: busca apoyo y dinero, no anuncia una aprobación ni se queja.

origin.text: Dear Ms Okafor, I am writing to put forward a proposal for a Saturday book swap in the library garden. The main benefit is tangible: children will get free books, and the library will reach families who rarely visit it. We outline a plan in two stages, and we recommend starting in May. We request a grant of 600 dollars to cover tables and posters. Several local shops already endorse the idea.

prompt.es: Según el correo, ¿por qué menciona Mia que varios comercios respaldan la idea?

choices.text: To explain that the shops will pay for the posters.
To show that the request has support in the neighbourhood.
To warn that the plan depends on the shops opening.

feedback.es: Endorse significa respaldar: al citar a los comercios, Mia sugiere que la petición cuenta con apoyo local; no dice que paguen nada.

origin.text: Dear Ms Okafor, I am writing to put forward a proposal for a Saturday book swap in the library garden. The main benefit is tangible: children will get free books, and the library will reach families who rarely visit it. We outline a plan in two stages, and we recommend starting in May. We request a grant of 600 dollars to cover tables and posters. Several local shops already endorse the idea.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quiere un beneficio tangible: verduras cada semana para cuarenta familias.»

feedback.es: Tangible benefit es la colocación para una ventaja concreta que se puede medir, como las cuarenta familias que reciben verduras.

origin.text: Good intentions will not persuade the council. It wants a ___ benefit, something it can measure, such as forty families receiving fresh vegetables every week.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Pedimos una subvención para cubrir el costo de los puestos.»

answer.text: We request a grant to cover the cost of the stalls

feedback.es: We request + lo que pides: la subvención va justo después del verbo y el fin se añade con to cover.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué da a entender la decisión de Leo sobre el presupuesto.

choices.text: That the neighbours were not interested in the figures.
That a pitch should cover every figure in the written proposal.
That a pitch should persuade, while the document carries the figures.

feedback.es: Leo dejó las cifras para el documento y usó el pitch para persuadir con el beneficio: cada formato cumple una función distinta; ni el público desconocía las cifras ni el pitch debía repetirlas.

origin.audio: At last night's meeting, Leo gave a five-minute pitch for a youth football league. He did not read the budget aloud. He said the written proposal, which everyone had received by email, contained every figure. Instead, he spent his time on the benefit, describing how the league would keep teenagers busy on Friday evenings.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador. ¿Qué parte de la propuesta falta todavía?

choices.text: The request for money or support.
The objective of the project.
The plan for the weekends of work.

feedback.es: El borrador tiene objetivo, beneficio, plan y recomendación, pero nadie pide nada todavía: falta la petición.

origin.text: Our objective is to paint the school gym with help from parents. The main benefit is a safer, brighter space for sport. We outline a plan with two weekends of work, and we recommend the first weekend of June.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por eso solicitamos una subvención de 1.500 dólares en el último párrafo.»

feedback.es: We request… es la fórmula de la petición y suele ocupar el último párrafo.

origin.text: A reader should always know what we are asking for. That is why we ___ a grant of 1,500 dollars in the final paragraph.

es: Usar recommend, suggest, propose e insist con el patrón correcto: -ing o that + sujeto + verbo base.

teaching.en: We recommend that the council approve the budget before the fifth of this month, since the stage must be booked before the prices rise again.
teaching.es: Recomendamos que el consejo apruebe el presupuesto antes del día cinco de este mes, ya que hay que reservar el escenario antes de que los precios vuelvan a subir.
teaching.explanationEs: Recommend that + sujeto + verbo base: approve, sin -s aunque el sujeto sea singular.
segments: We recommend that the council approve the budget before the fifth of this
month, since the stage must be booked before the prices rise again.
teaching.audioText: We recommend that the council approve the budget before the fifth of this month, since the stage must be booked before the prices rise again.

teaching.en: Mia and I suggest postponing the concert until the weather improves, but the chair would rather suggest that the committee postpone the vote until Friday.
teaching.es: Mia y yo sugerimos aplazar el concierto hasta que mejore el tiempo, pero el presidente prefiere sugerir que el comité aplace la votación hasta el viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest admite -ing (sin nuevo sujeto) o that + sujeto + verbo base, nunca to + infinitivo.
segments: Mia and I suggest postponing the concert until the weather improves, but the
chair would rather suggest that the committee postpone the vote until Friday.
teaching.audioText: Mia and I suggest postponing the concert until the weather improves, but the chair would rather suggest that the committee postpone the vote until Friday.

teaching.en: The rules stipulate that every volunteer wear a badge, and it is imperative that nobody enter the stage area without one.
teaching.es: Las normas estipulan que cada voluntario lleve una credencial, y es imprescindible que nadie entre en la zona del escenario sin ella.
teaching.explanationEs: Stipulate that e it is imperative that piden forma base: wear, enter, sin -s ni -ed.
segments: The rules stipulate that every volunteer wear a badge, and it
is imperative that nobody enter the stage area without one.
teaching.audioText: The rules stipulate that every volunteer wear a badge, and it is imperative that nobody enter the stage area without one.

teaching.en: It is advisable that visitors arrive early, and we propose that the gates open at noon so that the queues stay short.
teaching.es: Es aconsejable que los visitantes lleguen temprano, y proponemos que las puertas abran al mediodía para que las colas sean cortas.
teaching.explanationEs: It is advisable that + sujeto + forma base: un consejo más suave que imperative.
segments: It is advisable that visitors arrive early, and we propose that
the gates open at noon so that the queues stay short.
teaching.audioText: It is advisable that visitors arrive early, and we propose that the gates open at noon so that the queues stay short.

teaching.en: We insist on a written contract, and we insist that every sponsor sign it before the posters are printed.
teaching.es: Exigimos un contrato por escrito, y exigimos que cada patrocinador lo firme antes de imprimir los carteles.
teaching.explanationEs: Insist on + nombre o -ing; insist that + sujeto + forma base. Insist to + infinitivo no existe.
segments: We insist on a written contract, and we insist that
every sponsor sign it before the posters are printed.
teaching.audioText: We insist on a written contract, and we insist that every sponsor sign it before the posters are printed.

teaching.en: It is essential that the stage be ready by Friday, so the residents call for a daily inspection until the gates open.
teaching.es: Es esencial que el escenario esté listo para el viernes, así que los vecinos reclaman una inspección diaria hasta que se abran las puertas.
teaching.explanationEs: It is essential that… pide be en lugar de is; call for + nombre = reclamar o pedir algo.
segments: It is essential that the stage be ready by Friday, so
the residents call for a daily inspection until the gates open.
teaching.audioText: It is essential that the stage be ready by Friday, so the residents call for a daily inspection until the gates open.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta: «Recomendamos que el consejo apruebe el plan.»

choices.text: We recommend that the council approves the plan.
We recommend that the council approve the plan.
We recommend the council to approve the plan.

feedback.es: Tras recommend that el verbo va en forma base (approve), aunque el sujeto sea singular; recommend no admite «the council to approve».

hint.es: Fíjate en el verbo después de «the council»: ¿lleva -s?

origin.text: At the planning meeting, the chair asked each member for advice on the safety of the festival. One member wrote this sentence in the minutes.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia sugiere aplazar el concierto hasta la semana que viene.»

feedback.es: Suggest admite -ing cuando no hay nuevo sujeto: suggests postponing, nunca «suggests to postpone».

hint.es: Tras suggest, el verbo va en forma -ing.

origin.text: The forecast is very poor for Saturday, and the stage has no roof. Mia suggests ___ the concert until next week.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es imprescindible que nadie entre en la zona del escenario.»

answer.text: It is imperative that nobody enter the stage area

feedback.es: It is imperative that + sujeto + forma base: enter, sin -s.

hint.es: Empieza con la fórmula impersonal y deja el verbo en forma base.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué propone la presidenta sobre la decisión pendiente.

choices.text: Opening the gates at noon, as Sara proposed.
Adding two more guards before the committee meets again.
Waiting until Friday to decide, once the final price arrives.

feedback.es: La presidenta cierra con «suggested postponing the decision until Friday»; abrir al mediodía lo propuso Sara y los guardias los aconsejó la tesorera.

origin.audio: At the festival committee, the discussion got heated. Sara proposed that the gates open at noon, while Carlos insisted on keeping the original time of two o'clock because the sound check would not finish any earlier. The treasurer stipulated that nobody be admitted without a ticket, and she added that it was advisable to add two extra guards. In the end, the chair suggested postponing the decision until Friday, when the builder would send his final quote.

prompt.es: Completa: «El contrato estipula que cada escenario sea inspeccionado antes de abrir.»

feedback.es: Tras stipulate that el verbo va en forma base: be inspected, no is inspected.

origin.text: The council is strict about safety at open-air events. The contract stipulates that every stage ___ inspected before the gates open.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que expresa el autor.

pairs: We insist on a written contract.
It is advisable that visitors arrive early.
We propose that the gates open at noon.
The rules stipulate that volunteers wear a badge.

feedback.es: Insist on exige, advisable aconseja con prudencia, propose plantea una opción y stipulate fija un requisito oficial.

pairs: We insist on a written contract.
It is advisable that visitors arrive early.
We propose that the gates open at noon.
The rules stipulate that volunteers wear a badge.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Tom. ¿Qué exige el consejo sobre el escenario?

choices.text: An inspection of the structure on the day of the event.
Payment of the insurance on the day of the event.
An inspection of the stage before the fifth of the month.

feedback.es: El consejo pide que el escenario sea inspeccionado el mismo día; el seguro se paga antes del día cinco, que es la otra condición.

origin.audio: Hello, this is Tom from the festival office. I am calling because the council has set two conditions. It stipulates that the organisers pay the insurance before the fifth, and it is imperative that the stage be inspected on the day itself. Personally, I suggest that Mia handle the insurance, but I doubt that we can meet the second condition without postponing the opening by an hour.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué da a entender Tom sobre la segunda condición?

choices.text: That Mia will refuse to handle the insurance in time.
That meeting it could make the opening later than planned.
That the council may cancel the condition before Friday.

feedback.es: Tom duda de poder cumplirla «without postponing the opening by an hour»: cumplirla probablemente retrasará la apertura.

origin.audio: Hello, this is Tom from the festival office. I am calling because the council has set two conditions. It stipulates that the organisers pay the insurance before the fifth, and it is imperative that the stage be inspected on the day itself. Personally, I suggest that Mia handle the insurance, but I doubt that we can meet the second condition without postponing the opening by an hour.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los vecinos insisten en una hora de cierre a las diez.»

feedback.es: Insist on + nombre es la colocación para exigir algo: insist on a closing time.

origin.text: The neighbours are worried about the noise. They insist ___ a closing time of ten o'clock for every concert.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es aconsejable que todos lleguen temprano.»

answer.text: It is advisable that everyone arrive early

feedback.es: It is advisable that + sujeto + forma base: arrive, aunque everyone sea singular.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la autora ante el retraso de la votación?

choices.text: Ready to sign tonight if the members prefer to decide.
Against any decision being taken before the end of the month.
Firm that nothing be signed yet, but open about the date.

feedback.es: Pide con firmeza no firmar aún («advisable that nothing be signed») pero es flexible con la fecha («I do not insist on a fixed date»).

origin.text: Dear committee, I recommend that we postpone the vote, although I understand that some members would prefer to decide tonight. Since the insurance company has not replied, it is advisable that nothing be signed before we know the terms. I do not insist on a fixed date, but I would call for a decision by the end of the month.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato. ¿Con qué fin proponen los organizadores un voluntario para las salidas?

choices.text: To prevent another blocked exit during the event.
To avoid paying a fine for the delivery van.
To answer the official's request for more volunteers.

feedback.es: La propuesta responde al problema de la puerta bloqueada: un responsable fijo evitará que se repita; el texto no habla de multas ni de pedir voluntarios.

origin.audio: Last week the festival was almost closed down. The council had stipulated that the exits be kept clear at all times, but during the sound check a delivery van blocked the main gate. Nobody was hurt, yet an official insisted on a written apology and called for a full safety review. The organisers now propose that one volunteer be responsible for the exits throughout the event.

prompt.es: Completa: «Piensan reclamar una revisión completa antes de abrir las puertas.»

feedback.es: Call for + nombre significa reclamar o pedir públicamente algo.

origin.text: The residents are anxious about safety. They plan to call ___ a full review before the gates open.

es: Leer una propuesta con ojo crítico: detectar puntos débiles, riesgos y preguntas previsibles, y justificarlos.

vocabulary.es: evidente, que salta a la vista

teaching.en: The proposal is vague: it promises that «many families» will benefit, but it offers no evidence, no numbers and no dates.
teaching.es: La propuesta es vaga: promete que «muchas familias» se beneficiarán, pero no ofrece pruebas, ni cifras, ni fechas.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague = sin datos concretos. Se justifica con lo que falta: no evidence, no numbers.
segments: The proposal is vague: it promises that «many families» will benefit,
but it offers no evidence, no numbers and no dates.
teaching.audioText: The proposal is vague: it promises that «many families» will benefit, but it offers no evidence, no numbers and no dates.

teaching.en: Finishing the garden in two weeks is unrealistic with only three volunteers, and the glaring omission is that nobody has asked the owner of the land.
teaching.es: Terminar el huerto en dos semanas es poco realista con solo tres voluntarios, y la omisión más evidente es que nadie ha preguntado al dueño del terreno.
teaching.explanationEs: Unrealistic = plazo o meta imposible; glaring = un fallo que salta a la vista.
segments: Finishing the garden in two weeks is unrealistic with only three volunteers, and
the glaring omission is that nobody has asked the owner of the land.
teaching.audioText: Finishing the garden in two weeks is unrealistic with only three volunteers, and the glaring omission is that nobody has asked the owner of the land.

teaching.en: The whole plan rests on one assumption, that the council will pay, and both the schedule and the budget hinge on that promise.
teaching.es: Todo el plan se apoya en un supuesto, que el consejo pagará, y tanto el calendario como el presupuesto dependen por completo de esa promesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Rest on / hinge on an assumption: el plan depende de algo que nadie ha comprobado.
segments: The whole plan rests on one assumption, that the council will pay,
and both the schedule and the budget hinge on that promise.
teaching.audioText: The whole plan rests on one assumption, that the council will pay, and both the schedule and the budget hinge on that promise.

teaching.en: The authors overlook one risk: there is no contingency if the tools arrive late, and their sweeping claim that «everyone will help» is unsubstantiated.
teaching.es: Los autores pasan por alto un riesgo: no hay plan de contingencia si las herramientas llegan tarde, y su afirmación generalizadora de que «todos ayudarán» no tiene pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Overlook = no ver algo importante; sweeping y unsubstantiated describen una afirmación sin matices ni pruebas.
segments: The authors overlook one risk: there is no contingency if the tools
arrive late, and their sweeping claim that «everyone will help» is unsubstantiated.
teaching.audioText: The authors overlook one risk: there is no contingency if the tools arrive late, and their sweeping claim that «everyone will help» is unsubstantiated.

teaching.en: Is the plan feasible with a budget of only 500 dollars, or are we simply being too hopeful about what the volunteers can do?
teaching.es: ¿Es viable el plan con un presupuesto de solo 500 dólares, o simplemente somos demasiado optimistas sobre lo que pueden hacer los voluntarios?
teaching.explanationEs: Feasible = que se puede llevar a cabo en la práctica con los medios disponibles.
segments: Is the plan feasible with a budget of only 500 dollars, or
are we simply being too hopeful about what the volunteers can do?
teaching.audioText: Is the plan feasible with a budget of only 500 dollars, or are we simply being too hopeful about what the volunteers can do?

teaching.en: We should anticipate three questions from the council: who pays, who builds and who cleans up when the festival is over?
teaching.es: Deberíamos anticipar tres preguntas del consejo: quién paga, quién construye y quién limpia cuando termine el festival.
teaching.explanationEs: Anticipate = prever algo y preparar la respuesta antes de que lo pregunten.
segments: We should anticipate three questions from the council: who pays, who
builds and who cleans up when the festival is over?
teaching.audioText: We should anticipate three questions from the council: who pays, who builds and who cleans up when the festival is over?

prompt.es: Lee la observación del revisor. ¿Qué punto débil señala?

choices.text: The schedule is unrealistic for so few volunteers in two weeks.
The plan has no contingency for late deliveries of the tools.
The claim is sweeping and has no evidence behind it.

feedback.es: «Everyone will help» sin un solo nombre ni lista es una afirmación generalizadora y sin pruebas; no se habla de plazos ni de entregas.

hint.es: Piensa en qué falta: nombres y una lista que respalde «everyone».

origin.text: The authors write that «everyone in the neighbourhood will help», but they name nobody and give no sign-up list.

prompt.es: Completa: «Como no da cifras, es demasiado vaga para que el consejo la valore.»

feedback.es: Vague describe un texto sin datos concretos: «many families» no permite valorar nada.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo para un texto sin cifras ni fechas.

origin.text: The proposal says that «many families» will benefit. It gives no figures, so it is too ___ for the council to decide anything.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los autores pasan por alto un riesgo importante.»

answer.text: The authors overlook one important risk

feedback.es: Overlook + riesgo: los autores no han visto algo que debían haber visto.

hint.es: Empieza con el sujeto y deja el riesgo para el final.

prompt.es: Según la propuesta, ¿en qué supuesto se apoya todo el plan?

choices.text: That the council will pay for the tools and the soil.
That the school will lend the empty lot for two weeks.
That three volunteers can work through the night.

feedback.es: El texto dice «The council will pay for the tools and the soil» y por eso no hay presupuesto: todo depende de ese supuesto no comprobado.

origin.text: Green Corner Garden. Our objective is to build a community garden on the empty lot beside the school. Many families will benefit, and everyone in the neighbourhood has promised to help. We will finish the whole garden in two weeks with three volunteers. We will also paint the school gate. The council will pay for the tools and the soil, so we have not included a budget. If the tools arrive late, the work will simply continue the following week.

prompt.es: Escucha la valoración de Leo y elige qué riesgo cree que pasan por alto los autores.

choices.text: That the rain might last all night.
That the main band might cancel.
That the crowd might be larger than expected.

feedback.es: El riesgo olvidado es que cancele el grupo principal; la lluvia sí se menciona y el escenario solo aparece como un supuesto del presupuesto, no como un riesgo olvidado.
